diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $f \in C([0,1]^d)$ be given. There exist $n\in\N^+$ and affine maps 
$\mathcal{A}_{i},\, \mathcal{A}_{i}^{\mathrm{out}} \in \aff_{\le 5d}$ for $i=1,2,\cdots,n$  
such that, defining $f_1 \coloneqq f$ and
\[
   f_{k+1} \coloneqq f_k - \mathcal{A}_{k}^{\mathrm{out}} \circ 
   \ocomp_{i=1}^k (\ReLU \circ \mathcal{A}_i)\quad   \tn{for}\     k=1,2,\dots,n,
\]

Proceeding recursively, the same argument can be applied to 
$f_{n_1+n_2+1}, f_{n_1+n_2+n_3+1},$ and so on.

issues.failure_explanation: Applying the one-step theorem to the residual $f_{n_1+1}$ yields a standalone finite scheme with maps indexed $1,\dots,n_2$ and a fresh recurrence; it does not yield maps indexed $n_1+1,\dots,n_1+n_2$ satisfying the global recurrence with the previously frozen blocks composed in. The proof never establishes that the new blocks can be appended to the existing trunk (for instance, that the trunk output retains the original input $x$ so the new blocks can act on it). Thus the recursive step is not a valid inference as written.

failure_location.quote:
Next, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:main:mgdl:one:op} again to $f_{n_1+1}\in C([0,1]^d)$. 
There exist $n_2\in\N^+$  and affine maps 
$\mathcal{A}_{k}, \mathcal{A}_{k}^{\mathrm{out}} \in \aff_{\le 5d}$ for $k=n_1+1,\cdots,n_1+n_2$ 
such that, with 
\[
   f_{k+1} \coloneqq f_k - \mathcal{A}_{k}^{\mathrm{out}} \circ 
   \ocomp_{i=1}^k (\ReLU \circ \mathcal{A}_i)\\quad   \tn{for}\    k=n_1+1,\dots,n_1+n_2,
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and maintain the invariant that each trunk preserves the original input $x$ (as suggested by the identity map in the architecture figure), so the blocks produced by each one-step application can be appended to the existing trunk. This is a contained construction detail.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the main theorem does not establish the existence of a single infinite MGDL sequence with the required recurrence; the main theorem and its corollary are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Recursive application of the one-step contraction does not produce the required global MGDL recurrence
issues.why_classification: Requires a contained but nontrivial construction invariant to make the recursive application valid; the main result plausibly survives, but the proof as written has a genuine gap.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where \(T_1\) acts on the original input.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the stated ocomp definition, $\ocomp_{i=1}^k(\ReLU\circ\mathcal{A}_i)=(\ReLU\circ\mathcal{A}_1)\\circ\cdots\circ(\ReLU\circ\mathcal{A}_k)$, which applies $\mathcal{A}_k$ first. The proof of the one-step theorem instead constructs $h_k=\mathcal{A}_k^{\mathrm{out}}\circ(\ReLU\circ\mathcal{A}_k)\\circ\cdots\circ(\ReLU\circ\mathcal{A}_1)$, applying $\mathcal{A}_1$ first, matching the narrative that $T_1$ acts on the original input. Hence the proof does not establish the recurrence stated in the theorem; the formal composition order is inconsistent with the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the ocomp definition to $\ocomp_{i=1}^n f_i = f_n\circ\cdots\circ f_1$ (equivalently, write the compositions explicitly in application order). This one-line change aligns the theorem statements with the proof and the narrative.
issues.overall_effect: The one-step theorem's stated MGDL form is not what the proof constructs; the main theorem and corollary, which use the same ocomp convention, are affected.
issues.title: Composition order in the one-step theorem's proof contradicts the ocomp convention used in the theorem statements
issues.why_classification: A single forced notational correction restores consistency; the intended architecture and all substantive claims survive.

issues.failure_explanation: For $f\equiv0$, $M_f=0$, so $T_\varepsilon f\equiv0$ and every $h_k\equiv0$; hence $f_k\equiv0$ and $\|f_{k+1}\|_{L^p}=\|f_k\|_{L^p}=0$, contradicting the strict inequality. The theorems do not exclude the identically zero target, nor qualify the strict monotonicity to the nonzero case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $f\not\equiv0$ to the strict monotonicity statements, or state that the strict inequality holds whenever $f_k\not\equiv0$. A one-line degenerate-case fix.
issues.overall_effect: The strict $L^p$ decrease in the one-step theorem item (iii) and the main theorem item (ii) is false for $f\equiv0$; the convergence claims themselves remain valid.
issues.title: Strict L^p monotonicity fails for the identically zero target
issues.why_classification: A standard degenerate-case condition restores the strict claims; no substantive result or rate is lost.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the averaged $\Psi$ by a ReLU-representable cutoff that genuinely vanishes outside $rQ$, e.g., $\Gamma_Q(x)=\psi(\max_i |2(x_i-c_i)/\ell|)$ or an equivalent construction, and re-verify C1/C2 and the width-$5d$ network realization. issues.overall_effect: The verification of condition C1 for $T_\varepsilon$ (which sets $T_\varepsilon g=0$ outside the union of the dilated cubes) is false; $T_\varepsilon$ need not be a positive $\varepsilon$-contraction, so the one-step contraction theorem, the main MGDL theorem, and the corollary lose their proofs.
issues.title: Constructed cutoff function does not vanish outside the dilated cube for d>=2
issues.why_classification: The central cutoff construction is wrong for $d\ge2$; repairing it requires a new cutoff and re-verification of the contraction conditions, though the main results plausibly survive in corrected form.
